SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

medium adjective

of middle size or degree

also medium-sized, middle-sized, middling, moderate

classical

Caes. BC 3.46.1: mediocrī lātitūdine fossam
Caes. BG 5.44.6: mediocrī spatiō relictō

1mediocris: short o (Lewis & Short mediō̆cris, “ō usually; rarely ŏ”). De Vaan 424, s.v. ocris, prints mediocris without a macron and derives it from ocris, “rugged mountain” (PIE *h₂ok-r-i-): “orig. ‘situated at the middle, half-way of the top’”. In verse the vowel stands before cr, so the syllable can be heavy by position and the metre cannot show a long vowel (Hor. AP 370, 372).

mediocris1, mediocre

adjective, third declension

medium, middling, of moderate size

Between too much and too little (Cic. Off. 1.89, Lewis & Short). Of people and their gifts it can mean ordinary, mediocre (ōrātōrēs mediocrēs, Cic. Brut. 136); nōn mediocris is remarkable.

Examples

  • Mediocrī spatiō relictō Pullō pīlum in hostēs immittit

    Leaving a moderate distance, Pullo hurls his javelin at the enemyCaes. BG 5.44.6

  • intrā hās mediocrī lātitūdine fossam tēctīs mīlitibus obdūcī jussit

    behind these he had a trench of medium width dug, with the soldiers under coverCaes. BC 3.46.1

Other words

  • modicus, modica, modicum — moderate, of moderate size

    adjective · also used · classical · Traupman 205, 346 (of moderate size); Plin. NH 11.141: oculī modicī (Lewis & Short)

    Keeping to a measure; of size, moderate. It can also mean small, scanty (Lewis & Short).

See also size, big, tiny, average.
